findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, so passkeys are never set up on fresh logins
findings.body: The new helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, and it gates both `authenticate()` (line 115) and the error `challenge()` (line 137). On a normal first login `context.getUser()` is null, so `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is no longer invoked — before this PR the fill happened exactly in the user==null branch. Without it, the `enableWebAuthnConditionalUI` attribute and the WebAuthn challenge/rpId are never set, so the `webauth` form and the conditional passkey autofill (including discoverable-key auto-login) disappear from the initial login page; passkey login would only work during re-authentication. The condition is inverted: it should be true when the user is not yet known, and during re-authentication when the user actually has a passwordless credential, e.g. `user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(WebAuthnCredentialModel.TYPE_PASSWORDLESS)`. As written, the PR's own fresh-login tests (e.g. `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey`, which expects automatic login right after `oauth.openLoginForm()`, and the assertions that `//form[@id='webauth']` is present on the first login page in `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`/`passwordLoginWithExternalKey`) cannot pass.

findings.title: Call to no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method of that name in the class hierarchy is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, added in this PR. No no-arg overload exists in `UsernameForm`, `UsernamePasswordForm`, or `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, so the services module fails to compile. Presumably the call should be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys realm-wide instead of testing a user without a passkey
findings.body: The test is named and commented as verifying that a re-authenticating user who has no passkey is not offered passkey login (comment at line 304: "Passkeys login should not be available on the page as this user does not have passkey"), but it actually calls `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, disabling passkeys for the whole realm. In that setup `isPasskeysEnabled()` returns false and `fillContextForm` is skipped regardless of any per-user logic, so the test passes even though `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` never checks whether the user has a passkey credential (it only checks `user != null`). The actual scenario — realm with passkeys enabled, re-authenticating user with only a password, who should not see the WebAuthn conditional UI — is left untested, and with the current implementation that user would incorrectly get passkey elements rendered on the re-authentication page.
